context:
Goal: the gap backlog shrinks instead of growing.
Problem (rule): rule roles-findings-are-debts-or-notes files every finding, and gives it no owner, no expiry and no reader.
Based on (measured): since 2026-10-26, notes.md gained 1,304 lines and lost 358, so about 3.6 lines are added for each line removed. In the same time docs/debts/ added 107 debt files and deleted 37 (git on origin/main 174b005c1, 13:44 CST).
Based on (ruling): rule roles-findings-are-debts-or-notes: "A note becomes a debt after a real incident." Asked again because nothing counts incidents, so no note ever becomes a debt, and your 355 note asked how to work around the backlog.
Departs from: main, where a note waits with no end. The change adds a sighting count and an expiry to each note.

options.gain: Growth stops without relying on agents to remember. Each note carries `Seen: <date> x<n>`. A repeat sighting raises the count instead of adding a line, and a second sighting makes the note a debt. A note not seen for 30 days is deleted, and git keeps it. The janitor sweep runs this when asked, with no new process.
options.label: Sightings and expiry (recommended)
options.lose: A rare real gap seen only once is deleted after 30 days.

options.gain: Steady paydown. Each batch merge starts one lane that fixes the most-seen debt, and "debts opened vs closed" becomes a fifth pace number.
options.label: One debt-fix lane per batch
options.lose: One more lane per batch, and on its own it does not stop the growth.

options.gain: The pile cannot outrun the fixes. When open notes pass a budget, the next batch fixes debts only. The first ratchet run sets the budget number.
options.label: Over budget, the next batch is debt-only (recommended, with a)
options.lose: Feature lanes wait one batch whenever the pile grows past the budget.

short: Notes backlog: pick sightings and expiry, a paydown lane per batch, or both
title: How should the notes and debts backlog stop growing?
